findings.reason: the node would implement the reuse as written believing it is a pure dedup, and ship a serving-lane count that omits a lane the current code counts.
findings.text: §26 item 2 says `_serving_lanes` "groups the offered candidates by family, which `lane_context.lanes` already does", but `_serving_lanes` (reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py, §19 commit c2f7666a7) keys on `family or backend` while `lane_context.lanes` (reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:345) does `if lane is None: continue` and drops every candidate with no family; deriving the serving lanes from `lane_context`'s grouping therefore silently drops the backend-named lane a family-less candidate would have contributed, changing `serving_lane_count` and `hold_waits_for` — the exact facts §19 exists to put in front of Jev

findings.reason: the one clause that would catch the divergence has no subject once the change lands, so the section's own measure cannot show its guard fires.
findings.text: §26's done-when requires "a test fails if the two groupings diverge", but item 2's mechanism is to remove the second grouping ("derive the serving lanes from that one grouping"), so after item 2 is done there is no pair of groupings left to diverge and the control measures nothing
